logline: c. 5300 BC. After three years without rain, a desert tribe walks east toward the great river. Lions destroy them at a waterhole; a mother, Nebet, and her baby Wedja survive a sandstorm, shelter in a painted cave, and follow the water birds until the Nile saves them. Told by Nebet, years later, to her grown son.
narratorTone: quiet, fierce, tender with her son; still afraid of storms
narratorWhen: years later on the riverbank, telling her grown son Wedja how they survived
outline:
NARRATOR: Nebet, the mother, years later on the riverbank, telling her grown son Wedja how they survived.
WHEN: c. 5300 BC, just before the Predynastic, when the last rains failed in the Western Desert and its people drifted to the Nile.

For more than three years the rain did not come. The oasis where her family had always lived shrank to cracked mud, and the elders finally said what nobody wanted to hear: walk east, to the great river, or die here. So the whole tribe left: old people, children, the last thin animals, everything they could carry.

They walked for many days across the red land, Deshret. The water skins grew lighter. People stopped talking to save their breath. She carried her baby against her chest and counted the steps.

One evening, close to a waterhole, the lions came. They were starving too. It happened fast and it happened in the dark, and when it was over she was the only one still standing, her baby screaming in her arms. Everyone else was gone.

She ran until she couldn't, and then she walked. She was lost. Then the sky turned brown and a great sandstorm swallowed the world.

[SOUNDTRACK DROP] Inside the roar of the storm the story opens into a vision beyond her time: the gods that her descendants on the Nile will one day name, each appearing in their power: Ra the sun, Isis the protector of mothers, Sekhmet the lioness of fury, Amun the hidden wind, Osiris of death and rebirth, Horus the falcon sky, Thoth of knowledge, Anubis guide of the dead, Hathor of love and the sky, Ptah the maker, Nephthys mourner of the dead, Set lord of the desert storm, Bastet protector of the home, Maat of order and truth, Khnum who shapes children on his wheel, Sobek of the river's crocodiles. The song names them one by one.

She finds a cave in the rocks and crawls inside with the baby. In the dark the baby is terrified of the lizards on the walls. She calms him, sings to him, shows him the lizards are small and harmless. When the storm passes she lights a small fire. In its light they press their hands, hers and her baby's tiny one, against the rock and blow pigment around them, leaving their hand stencils beside the strange little "hands" already on the wall.

Days pass in the cave. The water is almost gone and there is no food. She knows that if she stays they will both die, so she wraps the baby to her chest and walks out into the desert one last time.

Outside, the desert is new after the storm: the old tracks are gone, the dunes have moved. She has no idea which way the river lies. On the second day she sees what the storm left behind: a few shallow pools in the hollows of the rock, the last rain the desert will give for a thousand years. She drinks, fills her skin, and above the pools she sees water birds circling and then flying east. Water birds don't fly toward nothing. She follows them.

Days of walking, always toward the morning sun, eating seeds and whatever the birds leave. When the water is gone again and she can walk no farther, she lies down in the shade of a rock with the baby on her chest. It is Wedja's crying that saves them: a band of herders, the last people from another dried-up oasis, driving a few cattle east toward the river, hear him in the silence. They give her milk and water and put her on their way.

From the crest of the last ridge they see it: a green line cutting the desert in two, wide water shining under the sun. Iteru, the river. Down on its banks live fishing and farming people. They take in the strangers; the river feeds everyone who reaches it.

ENDING (rebirth with opportunity): Nebet learns to fish the shallows and to cut the wild grain that springs up on the black mud the flood leaves behind. The desert took her people, but the river gives her a new one. Years later she sits on the bank with Wedja, grown and strong, his own children playing in the shallows, and tells him about the cave where their hands still rest on the wall beside the little 'hands' of the lizards. (Easter egg: hand stencils like these really were found in the Cave of Beasts in 2002.)

ACCURACY NOTE: in c. 5300 BC the people of the southern Nile were fishers, herders and wild-grain gatherers; sown farming appears a little later (Faiyum, from c. 5200 BC). The ending shows fishing and wild grain on the flood mud, not ploughed fields.

scenes.figures: men frozen lowering a long-horned cow into a clay-lined stone chamber; an elder with raised arms
scenes.location: the ceremonial ground near the stone circle
scenes.mg: the clay-lined pit and the men
scenes.narration: So we gave the sky our best cow, and buried her under a mound of stones. A gift is a kind of prayer.
scenes.sceneText: Herders lower their best cow into a clay-lined pit to beg for rain.
scenes.story: herders lower their best cow into a clay-lined pit to beg for rain
scenes.title: A Gift for the Sky

scenes.figures: nobody: only the mound and a dropped garland of dry grass
scenes.narration: The sky took the gift. It sent nothing back. The sky, I have learned, keeps what it is given.
scenes.sceneText: A fresh stone mound under a blinding cloudless sky.
scenes.story: a fresh stone mound under a blinding cloudless sky
scenes.title: The Rain Still Does Not Come

scenes.fg: packed hide bundles left on the ground
scenes.figures: a family frozen walking, a woman looking back over her shoulder
scenes.location: the southern edge of the lake basin
scenes.mg: the line of people and cattle
scenes.narration: The first families left that week. They drove their cattle south toward the hills, and I called them cowards.
scenes.sceneText: Families drive their cattle away south in a long line.
scenes.story: families drive their cattle away south in a long line
scenes.title: The First Families Leave

scenes.bg: the departing line of families in the distance

dialogue.line: Not yet. The herd is too weak.
dialogue.speaker: Amunharu

scenes.figures: his wife frozen pointing toward the departing families; Amunharu seated, frozen mid-stroke sharpening a chert spear point
scenes.narration: I wanted to wait.
scenes.sceneText: A woman watches families leave while her husband sharpens a spear.
scenes.story: a woman watches families leave while her husband sharpens a spear
scenes.title: Not Yet

scenes.bg: the dry playa under a dense starry sky

dialogue.line: Toward the sunrise. They say there is a river there that never dries.
dialogue.speaker: Amunharu

scenes.fg: the edge of an upright sandstone slab, a small fire in a ring of pebbles
scenes.figures: his wife frozen mid-turn toward him, one hand on a standing stone; Amunharu seated, looking up at the sky
scenes.location: inside the stone circle by the desert lake
scenes.musicNote: flute holds a long low note, crickets underneath
scenes.narration: On our last night we sat inside the circle of standing stones. They followed the sun and the seasons. But the seasons had changed.
scenes.sceneText: A couple sits inside a ring of standing stones under the stars on their last night.
scenes.story: a couple sits inside a ring of standing stones under the stars on their last night
scenes.title: Inside the Stone Circle

scenes.fg: the top edge of a standing stone
scenes.figures: nobody: only the stones
scenes.location: the sky above the stone circle
scenes.sceneText: The Milky Way turns slowly above the dark stones.
scenes.story: the Milky Way turns slowly above the dark stones
scenes.title: The Night Sky

scenes.bg: the grinding stone left behind in shadow
scenes.fg: a spear, a gourd and a small leather bag of grain
scenes.figures: Amunharu's hands frozen pulling a leather cord tight around a water skin
scenes.mg: the hands and the water skins
scenes.narration: We took only what we could carry: two water skins, my spear, a little grain. Everything else, we left to the sand.
scenes.sceneText: Hands tie water skins, a gourd and a small bag of grain.
scenes.story: hands tie water skins, a gourd and a small bag of grain
scenes.title: Only What They Can Carry

scenes.bg: the stone circle and grey sky
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen standing at the edge, an empty gourd hanging from his hand
scenes.mg: the wet mud where the pool was
scenes.narration: By morning, the last pool was mud.
scenes.sceneText: The last pool has become a patch of wet mud.
scenes.sfxNotes: a single bird call, then wind
scenes.story: the last pool has become a patch of wet mud
scenes.title: The Last Pool Is Mud

scenes.bg: the empty desert to the north-east under a rising sun
scenes.fg: the cracked rim of the basin
scenes.figures: a long line of families frozen mid-stride, cattle between them, Amunharu and his wife near the back
scenes.mg: the line of people and cattle
scenes.narration: The last families walked toward the sunrise together, with the herd between us.
scenes.sceneText: The last families walk toward the sunrise together with the herd between them.
scenes.story: the last families walk toward the sunrise together with the herd between them
scenes.title: Toward the Sunrise

scenes.fg: hot gravel and a dropped gourd
scenes.figures: a cow frozen with legs buckling; a herder frozen pulling its rope
scenes.location: a gravel plain beyond the lake
scenes.narration: Two days later, the cattle could barely stand. Neither could we.
scenes.sceneText: Exhausted cattle stand with their heads down in the heat.
scenes.story: exhausted cattle stand with their heads down in the heat
scenes.title: The Cattle Can Barely Stand

scenes.bg: dark rocks with a glint of water between them
scenes.figures: a young scout frozen mid-run, arm raised and pointing back toward the rocks
scenes.location: a rocky outcrop on the plain
scenes.narration: Then a scout came running. Water! A small pool, hidden between the rocks.
scenes.sceneText: A scout runs back shouting that he found water.
scenes.story: a scout runs back shouting that he found water
scenes.title: Water Between the Rocks

scenes.bg: rocks and tall dry grass glowing in the last light
scenes.figures: cattle frozen drinking; Amunharu frozen kneeling, splashing water on his face
scenes.mg: the cattle and people at the water
scenes.narration: At dusk we led the herd down to drink. For one evening, we were rich again.
scenes.sceneText: The herd drinks at a small waterhole while the people rest.
scenes.story: the herd drinks at a small waterhole while the people rest
scenes.title: Everyone Breathes Again

scenes.figures: a lean lion frozen crouched in the grass, eyes on the cattle
scenes.location: the tall grass beside the waterhole
scenes.sceneText: A lion's eyes in the tall grass, watching the herd.
scenes.story: a lion's eyes in the tall grass, watching the herd
scenes.title: Eyes in the Grass

scenes.bg: scattering cattle silhouettes against a blood-red sky
scenes.figures: a lean lion frozen mid-leap onto a longhorn cow; two herders frozen with throwing sticks raised; a man fallen in the dust
scenes.mg: the struggle at the water's edge
scenes.musicNote: bone clappers and skin drum in a violent pulse
scenes.narration: We were not the only ones who were thirsty. The lions had found the water first.
scenes.sceneText: Starving lions attack the herd at the waterhole while the herders fight back.
scenes.story: starving lions attack the herd at the waterhole while the herders fight back
scenes.title: The Lions Attack

scenes.bg: herders and cattle blurred in dust
scenes.fg: dust and a broken throwing stick
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen mid-thrust with a chert-tipped spear, face fierce; a lion frozen rearing
scenes.narration: We fought them with spears and throwing sticks. I remember the smell of that lion. I still dream it.
scenes.sceneText: Amunharu drives a spear at a lion.
scenes.story: Amunharu drives a spear at a lion
scenes.title: Spears and Throwing Sticks

scenes.figures: cattle frozen mid-stampede; people frozen running in different directions
scenes.location: the dark plain by the waterhole
scenes.musicNote: drums break into chaos, then cut
scenes.narration: The cattle broke and ran into the dark. So did we. I am not ashamed of it.
scenes.sceneText: Cattle and people scatter into the dark.
scenes.story: cattle and people scatter into the dark
scenes.title: Everyone Runs

scenes.bg: an empty sea of dunes, faint smoke from the night before
scenes.fg: a broken spear shaft half-buried in sand
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen mid-step, looking back; his wife frozen holding a water skin to her chest
scenes.location: the dunes east of the waterhole
scenes.mg: the couple on the dune crest, footprints scattering in every direction
scenes.musicNote: silence, then one breathy flute phrase
scenes.narration: By morning, our tribe was gone. Their tracks ran off in every direction, and none came back.
scenes.sceneText: A man and woman stand alone on a dune at dawn, the tribe scattered.
scenes.story: a man and woman stand alone on a dune at dawn, the tribe scattered
scenes.title: The Tribe Is Gone

scenes.figures: his wife frozen clutching a single goatskin water skin, eyes on the horizon
scenes.mg: his wife holding the skin, Amunharu beside her
scenes.narration: My wife and I were alone, with one water skin between us.
scenes.sceneText: A woman holds the couple's only water skin.
scenes.sfxNotes: wind, a soft slosh of water
scenes.story: a woman holds the couple's only water skin
scenes.title: One Water Skin

scenes.bg: the empty dunes east and west

dialogue.line: There is nothing to go back to.
dialogue.speaker: Amunharu

scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen pointing north-east toward the sunrise; his wife frozen looking back west
scenes.narration: We could have gone back. But back was only dust.
scenes.sceneText: The couple decides which way to walk.
scenes.story: the couple decides which way to walk
scenes.title: Nothing to Go Back To

scenes.bg: a shimmering horizon with cloud shadows
scenes.figures: the couple frozen mid-stride, his wife slightly ahead, Amunharu shading his eyes
scenes.location: the hard gravel plain between the lake and the river
scenes.musicNote: steady foot-stomp rhythm and hand claps
scenes.narration: So we walked toward the sunrise for days. The sun burned, and the ground was hot gravel.
scenes.sceneText: Two travellers cross a scorched plain.
scenes.sfxNotes: footsteps on gravel lock to the beat
scenes.story: two travellers cross a scorched plain
scenes.title: Hot Gravel

scenes.fg: a tiny fire of dry dung
scenes.figures: his wife frozen tipping the water skin to her lips; Amunharu frozen wrapped in a hide watching
scenes.location: a bare camp on the plain
scenes.narration: We drank only at night, a few sips at a time. The desert is cruel: burning days, freezing nights.
scenes.sceneText: The couple shares a few sips of water under the stars.
scenes.story: the couple shares a few sips of water under the stars
scenes.title: A Few Sips at Night

scenes.bg: a glittering mirage lake on the horizon
scenes.figures: the couple frozen, small, both staring at the horizon
scenes.location: the plain on the fourth day
scenes.musicNote: a false bright chord, then it fades
scenes.narration: On the fourth day, we saw a lake on the horizon. I ran toward it. It was not real.
scenes.sceneText: A shimmering lake appears on the horizon.
scenes.story: a shimmering lake appears on the horizon
scenes.title: A Lake That Isn't There

scenes.figures: his wife frozen on her knees; Amunharu frozen kneeling, holding her shoulders; an almost empty water skin
scenes.narration: The water skin was nearly empty, and my wife could not walk any farther.
scenes.sceneText: The woman collapses to her knees and the water skin is almost empty.
scenes.story: the woman collapses to her knees and the water skin is almost empty
scenes.title: She Cannot Walk Farther

scenes.bg: the north-eastern horizon and a faint line of golden dunes
scenes.fg: their long shadows on the gravel
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen mid-stride carrying his wife on his back, her arms around his neck
scenes.narration: So I carried her. She weighed less than a lamb by then.
scenes.sceneText: The man carries his wife on his back toward the east.
scenes.story: the man carries his wife on his back toward the east
scenes.title: He Carries Her

scenes.bg: ibis and egrets flying north-east across the sky
scenes.fg: dry ground with a few green weeds
scenes.figures: the couple frozen looking up, his wife pointing at the birds
scenes.location: the plain near the great dunes
scenes.narration: Then birds flew over us. Water birds. And water birds don't fly toward nothing.
scenes.sceneText: A flock of water birds flies overhead going east.
scenes.story: a flock of water birds flies overhead going east
scenes.title: Water Birds

scenes.bg: a broad river split by black granite boulders and green islands, palm groves and a small village on the far bank

dialogue.line: It's moving. A mirage doesn't move.
dialogue.speaker: Amunharu

scenes.fg: the knife-edge crest of a golden dune, wind lifting a plume of sand
scenes.figures: his wife frozen pointing down at the valley; Amunharu frozen on his knees beside her, one hand on the rock
scenes.location: the crest of the golden west-bank dunes above the Nile at the first rapids, near Abu
scenes.mg: the couple at the dune crest
scenes.musicNote: the whole palette opens: drone, flute, rattles, claps
scenes.narration: At last we reached the top of the great dunes. Below us lay a long green valley.
scenes.sceneText: From a dune crest, two exhausted walkers see the green Nile valley and the rapids for the first time.
scenes.sfxNotes: rising wind swell into distant river sound
scenes.story: from a dune crest, two exhausted walkers see the green Nile valley for the first time
scenes.title: The Top of the Dunes

scenes.bg: the broad river breaking around black granite boulders, green islands, small boats and village smoke
scenes.figures: nobody close: only tiny villagers and boats far below
scenes.location: the Nile at the first rapids seen from the dunes
scenes.mg: golden dunes sweeping down to green banks
scenes.narration: This was Iteru, the river you call the Nile.
scenes.sceneText: The Nile at the first rapids: black granite, white water, green islands.
scenes.story: the Nile at the first rapids: black granite, white water, green islands
scenes.title: The Nile

scenes.bg: black granite boulders and white rapids glowing in the sunset
scenes.fg: loose sand pouring down the slope
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen mid-slide down the sand, holding his wife's hand; she is caught mid-step behind him
scenes.location: the west-bank dunes running down to the first rapids
scenes.mg: the couple on the dune face
scenes.narration: We slid down the sand to the water, where black rocks break the river into rapids.
scenes.sceneText: The couple slide down a golden dune toward the rapids.
scenes.story: the couple slide down a golden dune toward the black rocks and the rapids
scenes.title: Down the Dunes

scenes.bg: the granite island of Abu across the water, reed huts, smoke
scenes.fg: split catfish drying on reed racks
scenes.figures: two fishermen frozen mid-turn holding a net between them; a woman frozen holding a black-topped red jar; the couple frozen at the edge of the camp
scenes.location: a fishing camp on the riverbank near Abu (Elephantine) at the first rapids
scenes.narration: Near the island of Abu, which you call Elephantine, fishermen stopped and stared at us. Two ghosts out of the desert.
scenes.sceneText: Fishermen near Abu stare at two dusty strangers.
scenes.story: fishermen stop and stare at two dusty strangers
scenes.title: Strangers at the Rapids

scenes.bg: reed huts, smoke and the river
scenes.figures: an old woman frozen holding out a flat loaf and a clay beer jar; his wife frozen reaching for it
scenes.mg: the old woman and the couple
scenes.narration: An old woman brought us bread and a jar of thick beer. I have never tasted better.
scenes.sceneText: An old woman offers the strangers bread and a jar of beer.
scenes.story: an old woman offers the strangers bread and a jar of beer
scenes.title: Bread and Beer

scenes.bg: black granite boulders and white water, a long boat on the river
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen kneeling with both hands in the river; his wife standing behind him; a fisherman frozen in a reed boat with his net half raised
scenes.location: the riverbank at the first rapids
scenes.narration: I knelt and put my hands in the water. It was cold, and it did not end.
scenes.sceneText: A desert man kneels with both hands in the Nile.
scenes.story: a desert man kneels with both hands in the Nile
scenes.title: Cold Water

scenes.bg: long boats pulled up on the bank, the river beyond
scenes.fg: rows of buff jars painted with red boats and wavy water lines, and black-topped red jars
scenes.figures: a woman potter frozen mid-stroke painting a red many-oared boat on a buff jar; a man frozen carrying a bundle of reeds; Amunharu's wife frozen watching, fascinated
scenes.narration: These were the river people. They farmed, made fine pots and built long boats. You call their world the Naqada culture.
scenes.sceneText: A potter paints a boat on a pale jar.
scenes.story: a potter paints a boat on a pale jar while others work around her
scenes.title: The River People

scenes.bg: mist on the river, granite boulders
scenes.fg: tusks and rolled hides on the bank
scenes.figures: two traders frozen lifting a bundle of hides into the boat; a trader frozen holding an elephant tusk; Amunharu frozen with one foot on the boat, his wife's hand on his shoulder
scenes.mg: the long high-prowed boat with two reed cabins and a branch at the prow, like those painted on Naqada pots
scenes.narration: A trading boat was leaving for the north with ivory and hides. They let us row for our passage.
scenes.sceneText: Traders load ivory and hides onto a long boat.
scenes.story: traders load a long many-oared boat with ivory and hides; the couple step aboard
scenes.title: A Boat Going North
scenes.weather: cool dawn mist on the water

scenes.bg: the wide river and green banks
scenes.fg: the boat's edge and an oar blade in the water
scenes.figures: Amunharu frozen gripping the boat's side with both hands, knuckles pale; his wife frozen beside him, half-smiling; rowers frozen mid-stroke
scenes.location: aboard the boat on the Nile
scenes.narration: Remember? I had never been on deep water. I held the side of that boat for three days.
scenes.sceneText: A desert man grips the side of a boat.
scenes.story: a desert man grips the side of a boat in fear while his wife almost smiles
scenes.title: Never on Deep Water

scenes.bg: villages, fields and herds on both banks, a huge low sun
scenes.figures: the rowers and the couple tiny on the boat, frozen
scenes.mg: the long boat small on the water
scenes.narration: The river carried us north. Villages, fields and herds slid past on both banks, more than I could count.
scenes.sceneText: A tiny boat drifts north on a vast river.
scenes.story: a tiny boat drifts north on a vast river between green banks
scenes.title: Downriver

scenes.bg: the mud-brick wall of Nubt with rectangular houses and smoke, cemeteries on the desert edge behind, a giant low sun
scenes.figures: the couple tiny at the boat's prow, frozen looking up
scenes.narration: Then a walled town rose above the fields. Nubt, the town you call Naqada. It became our home.
scenes.sceneText: A walled mud-brick town rises above the fields.
scenes.sfxNotes: town sounds rising over the water
scenes.story: a walled mud-brick town rises above the fields at the desert edge
scenes.title: Nubt

scenes.fg: tiny gold beads and a stone anvil
scenes.figures: a craftsman frozen mid-strike with a small stone hammer over a gold bead; Amunharu frozen in the doorway behind, carrying a load of reeds
scenes.narration: Nubt means 'the golden town'. Gold from the eastern desert passed through its gates, though none of it passed through my hands.
scenes.sceneText: A craftsman hammers a gold bead.
scenes.story: a craftsman hammers a thin gold bead over a stone anvil
scenes.title: The Golden Town

scenes.bg: the glowing river and boats under a violet sky
scenes.figures: the couple frozen side by side, her head on his shoulder, facing the river
scenes.location: the riverbank below Nubt at dusk
scenes.narration: We had lost our lake, our herd and our people. On this river, we began again.
scenes.sceneText: The couple stands as silhouettes against the river at dusk.
scenes.story: the couple stands as silhouettes against the river at dusk
scenes.title: Begin Again

scenes.bg: mud-brick roofs of Nubt and an enormous full moon over the river
scenes.card: Within about 300 years, the Naqada towns grew into the first kingdom of Egypt.
scenes.fg: a small fire and a painted jar
scenes.figures: old Amunharu frozen mid-gesture telling a story; three children frozen listening; an old woman, his wife, frozen smiling in a doorway
scenes.mg: the old man and the children
scenes.narration: I am old now. My grandchildren speak the river people's words, and they have never seen a cow starve. That is enough for me.
scenes.sceneText: An old man tells his story to children under a full moon.
scenes.story: an old man sits with children in a courtyard under a giant moon
scenes.title: Enough
scenes.weather: clear night, a huge full moon

sh_beats:
- the oasis shrinks; thin cattle, the last grinding of wild seed, dry lightning
- the elders decide to walk east to the river
- the march across the red desert; calves and old people fall behind
- a waterhole between rocks; starving lions attack in the night
- only Nebet and baby Wedja survive, alone with one water skin
- a sandstorm swallows them; a vision of the gods her descendants will name
- they shelter in a painted cave; Wedja fears the lizards; the little 'hands' on the wall
- fire; mother and baby leave their hand stencils in ochre
- days pass; the water runs out; Nebet walks out to find food
- the last rain pools in the rocks; water birds fly east and she follows them
- a mirage; she lies down to die in the shade of a rock
- Wedja's crying draws an eastbound herder band; milk and water
- from the last ridge they see the Nile
- the river people take them in; fishing and wild grain on the flood mud
- years later old Nebet tells grown Wedja the story
sh_cast: baby Wedja; Nebet's father and mother; the tribe; starving lions; an eastbound herder band; the river people
sh_culture: Saharan rock paintings (swimmers, headless beasts), ochre hand stencils, wordless chant, clay and gourd rattles, ochre face paint, eggshell beads
sh_danger: thirst, hunger, starving lions, the sandstorm, mirages, the empty desert
sh_egg: mother and baby's hand stencils beside the lizard 'hands', like the real ones found in the Cave of Beasts in 2002
sh_history: the Green Sahara dried around 5300 BC and its herders drifted to the Nile; the Cave of Beasts paintings; the 'little hands' made with reptile feet; life by the river before farming
sh_objects: ostrich-eggshell canteens and beads, grinding stones, chert blades, bows, leather water skins, long-horned cattle, fish-drying racks
sh_problem: no rain for three years; the oasis lake is dying and the tribe must walk east to the great river or die
sh_rebirth: the river people take them in; fishing and wild grain on the black flood mud; a new people by the river
sh_song: builds through the march and the lion attack; the bass drop hits the sandstorm, where the gods are revealed; the outro carries into the cave
sh_turn: the storm's last rain pools in the rocks and water birds lead her east; her baby's cry draws the herders
sh_when: c. 5300 BC, just before the Predynastic, when the Green Sahara dried
sh_where: a dying desert oasis → the red desert (Deshret) → a waterhole → the Wadi Sura cave in the Gilf Kebir → the Nile valley
sh_who: Nebet, a young herder mother; years later on the riverbank, telling her grown son Wedja how they survived

songPlace: The song builds through the march and the lion attack; the bass drop hits the moment the sandstorm swallows her, where the gods are revealed one by one; the outro carries into the cave
songTranslation:
(Hushing wind)
[Verse 1] Amun have mercy on us / save us. From the deadly Deshret / bring us. Grant us grace / save us. To our home.
[Chorus] Save me Ra / Isis / Sekhmet / Amun / Osiris / Horus / Thoth / Anubis / Hathor / Ptah / Nephthys / Set / Bastet / Maat / Khnum / Sobek.
[Verse 2] Save us / grant us grace. Bring us / to our home / from death. Amun / grant us grace. To our home / from death.
[Chorus, bass drop, outro] The same sixteen gods, rising to a choir climax, ending on Sobek.
theme: How the Nile saved lives when the deserts, and all hope, ran dry.
title: Ep 1 · Where the Nile Breathes Life
